title: FRONT BRAKE LINES
summary: Front brake lines: two pipes run from the master cylinder down to the brake warning switch (distribution/pressure differential switch) screwed to the LH frame rail; from the switch, pipes run to the LH front hose and across the front crossmember to the RH front hose. Pipes are held to the frame by clips and screws; each front flex hose is retained in its frame bracket by a spring clip and threads into the caliper with a copper washer.

fastening.to: master cylinder outlets (upper end) and switch [10] side ports (lower end)
fastening.note: Tube nuts of pipes [1] and [2] thread into the master cylinder at torque 5 and into the switch [10] at torque 1 (View A).
View A: screw [3] through the foot of the switch bracket into the frame.

fastening.to: switch [10] lower ports and front hoses [5]
fastening.note: Tube nuts of pipes [4] and [7] thread into the switch and into the hose fittings at torque 3.
Pipes are held by clips [8] each fastened with a screw [3] (torque 4) along the LH rail and across the front crossmember to the RH side.
Hose [5] fitting goes into the frame bracket and spring clip [9] slides in to retain it (View A).
Hose [5] lower end threads into the caliper with washer [6] (torque 2).

notes: Maximum allowable twist during asm. of front brake hoses is ± one notch at bracket.

With wheels straight ahead and suspension in full rebound, insert the hose into the frame bracket without kinking or twisting and install the retainer spring as shown; the paint stripe on the hose shows any kink or twist.
